title: Canonical point transport realizes shifted Weil pairings on cohomology
statement:
Fix distinct primes $p,\ell$, $a\ge1$, $q=p^a$, $k_0=\mathbf F_q$, an algebraic closure $k$ of $k_0$, a finite extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ inside a fixed $\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell$, and $\Lambda=E$ [def-weil-finite-field-fiber]. For a finite-type $k_0$-scheme $T_0$ set $T=T_0\times_{k_0}k$, $g_T=\operatorname{id}_{T_0}\times\operatorname{Spec}(\operatorname{Frob}_q)$ with geometric Frobenius, and $P_T=Lg_T^*$ [def-weil-frobenius-detailed, def-weil-derived-pullback-tensor-hom]. Work in the rational bounded constructible categories with Weil pairs $(M,\theta_M:P_TM\simeq M)$ and Weil arrows $u\theta_M=\theta_NP_T(u)$ [def-weil-weil-sheaf-complex]. All Weil isomorphisms below are arbitrary rational arrows; a Frobenius-stable integral lattice is not assumed.

Put $s=\operatorname{Spec}k$, $P=P_s$, and let $(A,\theta_A)$, $(D,\theta_D)$ be bounded constructible Weil point complexes. Use the point fiber functor $\operatorname{Fib}_s$ [def-weil-finite-coefficient-point] and its canonical transport $\iota_N:\operatorname{Fib}_sN\to\operatorname{Fib}_s(PN)$ [def-weil-frobenius-point-transport]. For every integer $r$ put $F_N=\operatorname{Fib}_s(\theta_N)\iota_N$, with the induced shift datum on $N[r]$. Let $c_s:P\Lambda_s\simeq\Lambda_s$ be the coefficient-unit datum [def-weil-frobenius-coefficient-twists], whose point Frobenius is $1$, and let $n\in\mathbf Z$. Suppose a morphism
$$B:A\otimes^LD[n]\to\Lambda_s$$
obeys the Weil equation
$$B(\theta_A\otimes\theta_{D[n]})\mu_{g_s}=c_sP(B),$$
where $\mu_{g_s}$ is canonical pullback tensor transport [def-weil-derived-pullback-tensor-hom]. The canonical point equivalence [lem-weil-point-fibre-equivalence] identifies $H^i(\operatorname{Fib}_sA)$ with $\operatorname{Hom}(\Lambda_s,A[i])$. Under it, for any representative $x:\Lambda_s\to A[i]$, the transported representative is $P(x)c_s^{-1}$ and its Frobenius representative is $\theta_A[i]P(x)c_s^{-1}$; the analogous formula holds for $D$.

Define $b_i:H^i(\operatorname{Fib}_sA)\times H^{n-i}(\operatorname{Fib}_sD)\to\Lambda$ by tensoring the two representatives and composing with $B$, using canonical shift, tensor and unit constraints. Then
$$b_i(F_Ax,F_Dy)=b_i(x,y),\qquad b_i(F_Ax,F_Dy)=c_sP(b_i(x,y))c_s^{-1}$$
with the second formula interpreted in $\operatorname{End}(\Lambda_s)$ under the point equivalence. These formulas use the canonical point transports, with the pullback tensor unit constraint identifying the two factors of $c_s^{-1}$ with the pullback of the unit tensor constraint. The formulas hold for all integers $i,n$, for zero objects, and for arbitrary rational Weil arrows. In particular, let $X_0$ be separated of finite type over $k_0$, $X=X_0\times_{k_0}k$, $a=a_X:X\to s$, and let $(K,\theta_K)$, $(L,\theta_L)$ be bounded constructible Weil pairs on $X$. If $A=Ra_!K$ with $\theta_A=Ra_!(\theta_K)\operatorname{FrEx}_{X,!}(K)$ and $D=Ra_*L$ with $\theta_D=Ra_*(\theta_L)\operatorname{FrEx}_{X,*}(L)$, the exchange maps of [def-weil-frobenius-cohomology-transport], then $F_A$ and $F_D$ are $\operatorname{Fib}_s(Ra_!\theta_K)\tau_{c,K}$ and $\operatorname{Fib}_s(Ra_*\theta_L)\tau_L$, the canonical compact-support and ordinary cohomology actions of that definition; the two support conventions are retained separately.

proof.text:
Finally substitute the two Weil data specified in the statement. Functoriality and [def-weil-frobenius-cohomology-transport] give separately
$$F_A=F(Ra_!\theta_K)F(\operatorname{FrEx}_{X,!}(K))\iota_{Ra_!K}=F(Ra_!\theta_K)\tau_{c,K},$$
$$F_D=F(Ra_*\theta_L)F(\operatorname{FrEx}_{X,*}(L))\iota_{Ra_*L}=F(Ra_*\theta_L)\tau_L.$$
Taking cohomology gives exactly the asserted compact-support and ordinary actions. These are two substitutions of the defining transports; no comparison between $Ra_!$ and $Ra_*$, and no properness hypothesis, enters.
